issues.should_be: Comprehensive chapter documenting binary data detection, binary modes, and flags
issues.fix_suggestion: Create complete chapter covering: (1) Binary detection concept and heuristics, (2) Three binary modes (Auto, SearchAndSuppress, AsText), (3) --binary flag behavior, (4) -a/--text flag behavior, (5) NUL byte detection, (6) Differences between implicit/explicit file search, (7) Memory map vs buffer-based binary detection, (8) Warning messages and output behavior

issues.description: No explanation of what binary detection is or why it exists
issues.should_add: Explain that binary detection is a heuristic process to identify and handle binary files differently from text files. Binary files often contain data unsuitable for textual pattern searching. Detection is based on finding NUL (\x00) bytes.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section explaining binary detection concept, mentioning that it's disabled by default in the searcher library but enabled by default in ripgrep's CLI for implicit file searches

issues.description: No documentation of the three binary modes: Auto, SearchAndSuppress, AsText
issues.should_add:
Document BinaryMode enum with three variants:
- Auto: Default mode, determines strategy based on whether file is explicit or implicit
- SearchAndSuppress: Search binary files but suppress matches and emit warnings when NUL bytes found
- AsText: Treat all files as text, no binary detection or special handling
issues.fix_suggestion: Create detailed section explaining each mode, when each is used, and the behavior differences. Include that Auto mode uses SearchAndSuppress for explicit files and quit-on-binary for implicit files

issues.should_add: Document --binary flag that causes ripgrep to search binary files with SearchAndSuppress mode. When enabled, ripgrep will search binary files and print warnings instead of silently skipping them. Only applicable for implicit (recursive) searches, not explicit file arguments.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section with examples showing --binary flag usage, explain it only affects implicit file searches (directory traversal), not explicit files or stdin. Show warning message format when binary data is detected

issues.should_add: Document -a/--text flag that disables binary detection entirely, treating all files as text. When used, ripgrep may print binary data to stdout including escape codes that could affect terminal behavior. Overrides --binary flag.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section explaining --text flag with warnings about potential terminal corruption, show examples of searching binary files as text, explain it overrides --binary

issues.description: No explanation of NUL byte (\x00) as binary indicator
issues.should_add: Explain that binary detection uses NUL bytes as the primary heuristic. When a NUL byte is encountered, the file is considered binary. This is a simple but effective heuristic since text files rarely contain NUL bytes while binary files typically do.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section explaining NUL byte detection, mention it's imperfect but practical, note that NUL bytes are searched for in buffer contents (buffered search) or in first few KB + matches (mmap search)

issues.description: No explanation of how binary detection differs between buffered and memory-mapped search
issues.should_add:
Document two different binary detection strategies:
1. Buffered search (--no-mmap): NUL bytes detected in all buffer contents as they're read
2. Memory-mapped search (--mmap): NUL bytes only searched in first ~64KB and in matching lines
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section explaining the two strategies, why they differ (memory efficiency vs thoroughness), include examples showing different behavior with --mmap vs --no-mmap

issues.description: No explanation of different behavior for implicit (recursive) vs explicit file arguments
issues.should_add:
Document that binary filtering behaves differently for implicit vs explicit files:
- Implicit (via -g glob or recursive): Binary files silently skipped, no output
- Explicit (file argument): Binary matches reported with 'binary file matches' message
The --binary flag makes implicit files behave like explicit ones.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section with side-by-side examples showing behavior differences, explain rationale (implicit searches favor precision, explicit searches favor recall)

issues.description: No documentation of binary detection warning message formats
issues.should_add:
Document the various warning messages:
- 'WARNING: stopped searching binary file after match (found "\0" byte around offset N)' for implicit files
- 'binary file matches (found "\0" byte around offset N)' for explicit files
- Different output for stdin searches
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section showing example warning messages for each scenario, explain what each means and when it appears

issues.description: No documentation of known edge cases and limitations
issues.should_add:
Document known issues:
1. With -l/--files-with-matches, binary files may be listed before NUL detected (performance optimization)
2. With --quiet, binary detection may be skipped for same reason
3. With --count, full file scan happens so binary detection works correctly
4. Matches occurring in same buffer as NUL byte (but before it) may not be printed
issues.fix_suggestion: Add troubleshooting section documenting these edge cases with examples from tests/binary.rs, explain they're acceptable tradeoffs for performance

issues.description: No documentation of BinaryDetection configuration for library users
issues.should_add: For users of the grep-searcher library, document BinaryDetection::none(), BinaryDetection::quit(byte), and BinaryDetection::convert(byte) methods. Explain that binary detection is disabled by default in the library (unlike the CLI).
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section for library users explaining how to configure binary detection in SearcherBuilder, mention difference between CLI defaults and library defaults

issues.description: No discussion of performance implications of binary detection
issues.should_add:
Explain performance tradeoffs:
- Binary detection adds minimal overhead (single byte search)
- Can significantly improve performance by skipping binary files early
- With --text, no detection overhead but may search irrelevant data
- Memory map mode has different detection characteristics for efficiency
issues.fix_suggestion: Add brief performance section explaining the tradeoffs and when to use each mode
